extracted.intended_audience: Authors and editors preparing Cochrane systematic reviews of interventions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and maintaining Cochrane systematic reviews on the effects of healthcare interventions, including planning, study selection, data collection, risk-of-bias assessment, analysis, GRADE, and interpretation. Also covers specialized topics (non-randomized studies, adverse effects, equity, economics, etc.) and links to MECIR core standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning a review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a standard method applicable to every review; the Handbook provides detailed guidance on how to plan a Cochrane systematic review of interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching and selecting studies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as a core standard area for every review; the Handbook describes methods for designing and executing searches and for selecting studies for inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the standard methods applicable to every review; includes guidance on extracting and managing study data for Cochrane reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias assessment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named as a standard method for every review; the Handbook provides approaches and tools for assessing risk of bias in included studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core methodological area for reviews; the Handbook covers statistical methods for meta-analysis and other quantitative syntheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among standard methods; the Handbook gives guidance on using GRADE to assess the certainty of evidence and to inform interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting results
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the standard methods applicable to every review; includes guidance on drawing conclusions and discussing implications of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-randomized studies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook includes specialised guidance for reviews that include non-randomized studies of interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse effects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialised topic guidance on identifying, extracting, and synthesising information about harms and adverse effects of interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex interventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on dealing with interventions that have multiple interacting components, contextual variability, and implementation considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialist guidance on considering equity (e.g., differential effects across populations) within systematic reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on incorporating economic evidence or considerations into intervention reviews, where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient-reported outcomes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialised guidance on measurement, extraction, and synthesis of outcomes reported directly by patients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual patient data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on conducting reviews or meta-analyses that use individual participant (patient-level) data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on planning and conducting prospective meta-analyses (where studies are prospectively identified and combined).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialist guidance on integrating qualitative evidence or methods within systematic reviews of interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological Expectations for Cochrane Intervention Reviews (MECIR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key aspects of Handbook guidance are collated as the Methodological Expectations for Cochrane Intervention Reviews (MECIR). These provide core standards that are generally expected of Cochrane reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each MECIR item includes a link to a relevant Handbook chapter; MECIR items are the core standards reviewers are generally expected to meet when preparing Cochrane intervention reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to cite the Handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: To cite the full Handbook online, please use: Higgins JPT, Thomas J, Chandler J, Cumpston M, Li T, Page MJ, et al, editor(s). Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5 (updated August 2024). Cochrane, 2024. Available from www.cochrane.org/handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also provides citation format for the print edition and notes that details for citing individual chapters are available in each chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to re-use Handbook material (academic/non-commercial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic or other non-commercial re-use of Handbook material: You do not need to request permission to use short quotations (though these must be appropriately cited), or to cite the Handbook as a source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reproducing material using screenshots, exact figures or tables, or lengthy direct quotations (more than 5 lines of text), you must fill in a form to request permission; approvals, if granted, are free of charge on condition that the source is acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to re-use Handbook material (commercial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial re-use includes any use of the Handbook that will be used in a product for which there is a monetary fee, and/or where it is associated in any way with any product or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For commercial reuse enquiries contact Wiley Global Permissions, John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.; commercial reuse is handled separately from academic/non-commercial requests.
